mechanism_narrative: The strong recovery in workplace mobility from t-2w to t-0w, indicating a return to office routines, will directly increase weekday foot traffic to retail and recreation establishments, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in transit station activity, specifically a week-on-week increase exceeding 10 points, signals increased commuting and general movement, which will subsequently boost retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises by more than 10 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The observed inverse relationship between declining residential mobility and increasing workplace mobility suggests a fundamental shift from home-based activities to out-of-home activities, which will collectively drive up retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to fall while WORKPLACES mobility rises, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the previous 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The current low and declining parks mobility, typical for the winter season, indicates a shift of leisure activities indoors, which will divert recreational spending towards retail and indoor recreation venues, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility remains low or declines further, but RETAIL_REC does not show an upward trend over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The observed slow but steady recovery in RETAIL_REC over the last two weeks (from -31.1 to -24.6), despite starting from a low point, suggests underlying demand for retail and recreation activities that will continue to push mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If grocery and pharmacy mobility stabilizes above 10% change from baseline for two consecutive weeks, it indicates a return to routine essential errands, freeing up time and confidence for non-essential retail and recreation, leading to a positive impact on RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes above 10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes above 10% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: A combined increase in both transit station and workplace mobility signifies a robust return to daily commuting and out-of-home activities, creating a synergistic effect that will strongly boost retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increase week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If residential mobility remains elevated above 10% change from baseline for two consecutive weeks, it suggests continued preference for home-based activities or caution, which will suppress visits to retail and recreation venues, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the previous 28 days.
